paper.title: Scalable Simulation of Strongly Correlated Fermions with Neural Gaussian Tensor Networks
paper.authors: Runze Chi, Ao Chen, Garnet Kin-Lic Chan

results.system_description: Hubbard model on the periodic 16 x 4 square lattice, U/t = 8, t' = 0, 56 electrons (28 up, 28 down), 1/8 hole doping
results.variant: N_v = 3, evaluated with the eight-image projection over mirror reflections in x and y and spin inversion
results.source_location: Supplemental Table tab:energy-16x4, row "NN-GPEPS, N_v = 3", columns E/N and sigma^2/N
results.eligibility_evidence: Variational energy per site of the authors' own neural-network Gaussian PEPS, measured at fixed parameters by VMC after optimization; not a training average or an extrapolation.
results.notes: H = -t sum_<ij>,s (c+c + h.c.) + U sum n_up n_down, t = 1, U = 8, each bond once, periodic 16 x 4 lattice (Eq. eq:hubbard); (N_up, N_down) = (28, 28), 1/8 hole doping (Table tab:recipe). A residual CNN maps the occupation configuration to the local matrices of a Gaussian fermionic PEPS with N_v virtual modes, contracted exactly (hybrid). Fixed-parameter measurement with FP32 CNN products and FP32 contraction; configurations exceeding the delay capacity get zero amplitude in both sampling and evaluation, so the estimate is the variational energy of that state, and none exceeded it in the reported runs (App. "Training and measurement"). The error is the largest block-jackknife standard error over blocks of 1, 2, 4 and 8 batches. The variance is the printed local-energy variance per site. The training-window means of Table tab:energy-source and the joint zero-variance extrapolation are not entered. Rows of other methods in the same table are quoted.
